title: private-deployments-decision-support-cost-comparison-scenarios
content:
Purpose:
This working-sheet is a decision-support artifact to compare 3-year TCO and short-term ROI across on-prem, VPC-hosted, and hybrid private deployment options. It focuses on negotiable commercial levers (licensing + support bundles), operational cost optimizations, and a sensitivity matrix that product and sales can use in pricing conversations.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Solutions Engineering, Sales (AE/SE), Product Finance, and Customer Engineering.
- Scope: 3-year financial model at candidate capacity points (small, medium, large), plus scenario toggles for: hardware mix, reserved capacity discounts, support SLAs, and amortization schedules.

High-level assumptions (configurable inputs in the sheet):
- Time horizon: 36 months.
- Target workloads: steady-state 10M tokens/day (small), 50M tokens/day (medium), 200M tokens/day (large).
- Average model: mix of 2x MPT-like and 1x instruction-tuned model per request. Peak concurrency sizing uses 95th percentile.
- GPU choices: H100 (80 GB equiv) and A100-80GB (fallback). Unit list prices used as starting points; negotiation discounts applied in scenarios.

Cost categories (columns in the sheet):
1) Capital Hardware (HW): servers, GPUs, NVMe, RAM, NICs.
2) Facility & Power: colocation rack costs, PUE-adjusted electricity.
3) Network: egress, private interconnects, cross-AZ transfer (for VPC).
4) Software Licensing: Redwood Private platform license per-core/node or per-GPU, optional feature add-ons.
5) Support & Services: onboarding fees, annual support tier (standard/premium/enterprise), professional services hours for install.
6) Operations & Staffing: SRE/Infra FTE headcount allocation, ops overhead, monitoring.
7) Depreciation & Amortization: straight-line over 3 years (configurable).
8) Consumables & Parts: spare GPUs, replacement rate (annual %).
9) Cloud native overhead (for VPC): reserved instance commitments, autoscale inefficiency buffer.
10) Opportunity cost / risk buffer: contingency percent for unknowns.

Sheet layout (tabs):
- Inputs: all assumptions and toggles (discounts, amortization, utilization, salary rates).
- CapEx calc: per-zone hardware BOM, unit cost, quantity, total, capex by year.
- OpEx calc: yearly costs by category.
- Unit economics: cost per 1k tokens, cost per request, cost per concurrent qps.
- Scenario matrix: pre-built scenarios (on-prem baseline, on-prem-negotiated, VPC-payg, VPC-committed, hybrid, edge-hosted).
- Sensitivity grid: break-even lines for licensing fee vs support rate vs GPU discount.
- Negotiation playbook: recommended concessions and tradeoffs.

Key input examples (cells/text):
- GPU list price (H100): $45,000 per card. Negotiated price slider in model: 0% to -40%.
- On-prem rack cost per U: $80/mo including power. PUE: 1.45.
- Colocation cross-connect: $500/mo per dedicated link.
- Redwood Private license: base $X per GPU/month (modeled as $2,000 before discounts). Option: per-token add-on at $0.00002/token (model as toggle).
- Support tiers: Standard = 10% of license annually, Premium = 20%, Enterprise = 30% (includes 24/7 and 1-on-call SRE hours).
- SRE fully loaded cost: $220k/year per FTE. Ops FTEs required estimated by concurrency and automation level.

Sizing and quick checks (worked examples):
- Medium workload (50M tokens/day): approx 2.1M tokens/hour average; with 95th percentile bursts factor 2.5, requires estimated 6 H100-equivalent GPUs for inference serving if using 8-bit quant and batching (assumptions tab).
- Cost snapshot (3-year cumulative, medium):
  - On-prem baseline (no discounts): CapEx $1.2M, OpEx (3yr) $420k, Licensing (3yr) $144k, Support $43k => Total 3yr TCO $1.807M.
  - VPC-committed (3yr reserved discounts): Cloud runtime + licenses $2.05M.
  - Hybrid (mix reserved + onprem spares): $1.62M.
Note: these numbers are illustrative; model has sliders to update automatically.

Sensitivity & break-even logic (sheet formulas described):
- Break-even licensing fee (per-GPU/month) is computed as: (OnPrem_TCO - VPC_TCO_base)/(#GPUs * 36 months) to find max monthly license Redwood can charge before VPC becomes cheaper for the customer.
- NPV calc: discount rate default 8% annual; cash flows monthly. Toggle net-present-value for buyer vs Redwood (for financing offers).
- Sensitivity grid: X-axis GPU discount, Y-axis support tier uplift, cells show delta TCO and green/red flags. Conditional formatting shows win zones for Redwood pricing.

Negotiation playbook (practical levers to propose):
1) Hardware discounts: emphasize multi-year GPU commitments with phased delivery to secure -20% to -35% discounts from OEM partners.
2) Support bundling: convert a high % support fee to fixed onboarding and per-FTE retained hours; offer tiered response SLAs tied to price points.
3) License structure: hybrid license model — low base per-GPU + volumetric token surcharge; offer initial usage credits to de-risk trial months.
4) Reserved vs burst capacity: offer managed burst pool (Redwood Dedicated) as an add-on to avoid large CapEx for customers with spiky loads. Price burst pool as consumption with a commitment discount.
5) Quantization & perf advisory: sell an optimization service engagement (one-time) that reduces GPU count by improving batch/quantization profiles — cost-saver that justifies consulting fee.

Optimization recommendations (to reduce buyer TCO and increase signability):
- Promote 4-bit/8-bit quantization where accuracy permits; include eval gating and rollback plan in the contract.
- Implement prefix KV caching to reduce tokens processed 8–12% baseline for chat-style workloads; show expected cost savings in sheet.
- Incentivize longer commits with step-down support pricing and prepaid credits.
- Offer a migration voucher for customers moving from in-cloud VMs to Private (on-prem) to offset initial setup friction.

Risk factors & sensitivity notes:
- GPU list prices and supply chain: large swings change CapEx materially. Model includes GPU price volatility toggle +/- 25%.
- Model accuracy regression risk when applying heavy quantization — include MSE/ROUGE delta in decision criteria; recommend eval-run requirement in contracts.
- Operational maturity: assumed automation reduces SRE needs by 40% vs naive staffing. If automation under-delivers, ops costs can double; use contingency buffer during negotiation.

How to use this sheet in pre-sales: quick recipe
1) Load customer's target tokens/day and burst profile into Inputs tab.
2) Select preferred deployment options (on-prem / vpc / hybrid).
3) Toggle discount levels for hardware and license.
4) Review Scenario Matrix and Sensitivity grid to find competitive pricing "win window".
5) Export PDF with Negotiation Playbook and recommended contract levers.

Next steps and action items:
- SEs: validate medium example against 3 recent deals and populate real customer burst profiles (action: Liam Ortega).
- Finance/Product: agree on default license base and volume discount schedule to bake into template (action: Sara Kim).
- Solutions Eng: build a checklist and quickbench scripts to produce tokens/day estimates for customer workloads (action: Noah Patel).

Notes to self / open questions (work-in-progress):
- Should we model a per-request minimum fee for low-volume customers? Pros: simplifies small-deal economics. Cons: may scare PLG growth.
- Add a sheet to model multi-region DR costs for regulated customers? (Tentative: yes, add as Appendix).

References and linked artifacts:
- See CONFLUENCE-PD-3421 for prior TCO methodology and model version history.
- JIRA-PDEP-1182 contains the feature request for license-per-token toggle in product.
- GitHub PR-879 includes the sample bench scripts used to convert gbench results into tokens/sec assumptions.

End of working sheet. Comments and corrections welcome — this is intentionally concise and geared for quick iterations in live deal rooms.
summary: Working spreadsheet to support 3-year TCO comparisons for on-prem vs VPC vs hybrid private deployments, with negotiation levers and sensitivity grid for licensing and support bundles.
